card.name: Two drugs given together, before a pair is named
card.fires_on: Words in sentences about two things acting or being given together, such as concurrently, Y-site, or the risk of combined use. It also fires at points where a second item or a pair is about to be referred to.

modes.label: Co-administration wording
modes.description: Words about giving two drugs together, like concurrently, co-administration, or Y-site.
modes.example: There are no data with ampicillin and sulbactam and allopurinol administered<< concurrently>>.

modes.label: Combined-use risk statements
modes.description: Words in interaction sentences where two drug classes together raise a risk.
modes.example: Concomitant use can increase the<< risk>> of bradycardia.

modes.label: Lists or pairs outside drug text
modes.description: Words inside general-text enumerations of two or more items, such as laws or steps.
modes.example: The incident, reflected ray, and the normal are in the same<< plane>>.

card.writes: It suppresses words meaning both, the former, or the latter, so it seems to lower the odds of a pair being summed up in those words.
card.plain: It lights up when the text is talking about two things used or occurring together, such as two drugs given at the same time.
